content.text: Journal playback does NOT function correctly.
Running system tests (config B) with journalling enabled works OK, but the resulting journal file cannot be played back successfully on an empty repository.
Specifically, on modification of demo:MultiOwnerObject from journal entry:
PDP is evaluating modifyObject request from journal playback to "not applicable".   It looks like the PDP is not asking for certain attributes when playing back from journal.  For example

So.. it appears that the PDP is not requesting the value of the urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:owner attribute in the journal playback case Had it requested the attribute, the request would have been logged.   The request context in both cases is the same:

It looks like the authz problem is ultimately due to a missing policy upon journal replay.  Policy 'permit-if-owner.xml' matched during the live run, but wasn't present in the journal replay run.  Looks like this policy (among others) is loaded at runtime, then later removed as part of a junit test.  Since policies may be stored/managed externally, they don't fall under the journalling umbrella.

Thus, I'm wondering if policy evaluation is appropriate for journal replay at all.   Since the existence of a journal entry implies that an operation successfully passed the policy evaluation, there really is no point in re-evaluating the policies upon replay. At best, it will succeed at slightly increasing the entropy of the universe.  At worst, fail (as we've seen).  Thus, it may be worthwhile to see if it's easy to disable policy evaluation at journal replay...  that would be the most straightforward thing to do.
Presumably, just due to missing managementDelegate marker interface.

comments.body:
[Issue Migrated from Sourceforge Task]
Task Submitter: birkland
Task #: 150858
SF URL: http://sourceforge.net/pm/task.php?func=detailtask&group_id=177054&group_project_id=53865&project_task_id=150858

Journal playback does NOT function correctly.

Running system tests (config B) with journalling enabled works OK, but the resulting journal file cannot be played back successfully on an empty repository.

Specifically, on modification of demo:MultiOwnerObject from journal entry:

2008-10-06T17:15:34.171-0400: PROBLEM: fedora.server.errors.authorization.AuthzDeniedException:
at fedora.server.security.PolicyEnforcementPoint.enforce(PolicyEnforcementPoint.java:458)
at fedora.server.security.DefaultAuthorization.enforceModifyObject(DefaultAuthorization.java:1284)
at fedora.server.management.DefaultManagement.modifyObject(DefaultManagement.java:182)
at sun.reflect.GeneratedMethodAccessor60.invoke(Unknown Source)
at sun.reflect.DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl.invoke(DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl.java:25)
at java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(Method.java:585)
at fedora.server.messaging.NotificationInvocationHandler.invoke(NotificationInvocationHandler.java:70)
at $Proxy0.modifyObject(Unknown Source)
at fedora.server.management.ManagementModule.modifyObject(ManagementModule.java:399)
at fedora.server.journal.managementmethods.ModifyObjectMethod.invoke(ModifyObjectMethod.java:26)
at fedora.server.journal.entry.ConsumerJournalEntry.invokeMethod(ConsumerJournalEntry.java:34)
at fedora.server.journal.JournalConsumerThread.run(JournalConsumerThread.java:84)

PDP is evaluating modifyObject request from journal playback to "not applicable". It looks like the PDP is not asking for certain attributes when playing back from journal. For example

Live:
(ResourceAttributeFinderModule) ResourceAttributeFinder.getAttributeLocally using ownerIdSeparator==[,]
(ResourceAttributeFinderModule) got urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:owner= [fedoraAdmin] [testuser1]
(AttributeFinder) urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:owner += fedoraAdmin
(AttributeFinder) urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:owner += testuser
(ResourceAttributeFinderModule) got urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:state=A
(AttributeFinder) urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:state += A
(AttributeFinder) fedoraRole += administrator

Journal:
(ResourceAttributeFinderModule) got urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:state=A
(AttributeFinder) urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:state += A
(AttributeFinder) fedoraRole += administrator

So.. it appears that the PDP is not requesting the value of the urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:owner attribute in the journal playback case Had it requested the attribute, the request would have been logged. The request context in both cases is the same:

<Attribute AttributeId="urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:pid" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue>demo:MultiOwnerObject</AttributeValue></Attribute>
<Attribute AttributeId="urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:resource:object:namespace" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue>demo</AttributeValue></Attribute>
<Attribute AttributeId="urn:oasis:names:tc:xacml:1.0:resource:resource-id" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue></AttributeValue></Attribute>
</Resource>
<Action>
<Attribute AttributeId="urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:action:api" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue>urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:action:api-m</AttributeValue></Attri
bute>
<Attribute AttributeId="urn:oasis:names:tc:xacml:1.0:action:action-id" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue></AttributeValue></Attribute>
<Attribute AttributeId="urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:action:contextId" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue>1521</AttributeValue></Attribute>
<Attribute AttributeId="urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:action:id" DataType="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string"><AttributeValue>urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:action:id-modifyObject</AttributeValu
e></Attribute>
</Action>
</Request>

It looks like the authz problem is ultimately due to a missing policy upon journal replay. Policy 'permit-if-owner.xml' matched during the live run, but wasn't present in the journal replay run.
